```{r setup, include = FALSE}
# Root locator + dual-load idiom shared with the tour and the bench drivers:
# the source tree (check and site-build contexts) loads through pkgload; a
# bare installed package (reader-side) loads through library().
.pkg_root <- function() {
  for (dd in c(".", "..", "../..")) {
    if (file.exists(file.path(dd, "DESCRIPTION")) &&
        file.exists(file.path(dd, "R", "treatment-report.R"))) return(normalizePath(dd))
  }
  NA_character_
}
PKG <- .pkg_root()
if (!is.na(PKG) && requireNamespace("pkgload", quietly = TRUE)) {
  suppressWarnings(suppressMessages(pkgload::load_all(PKG, quiet = TRUE,
                                                      export_all = TRUE)))
} else {
  library(msuiter)
}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
# The five-minute path runs against committed test bytes only: the specimen
# fixture (tests/testthat/fixtures/sigprofiler_sbs96_specimen.txt) plus the
# bundled reference face shipped inside the package. No downloads, no real
# data -- the claims-are-measured law of the docs/site lanes.
FIX <- local({
  if (is.na(PKG)) stop("fixture face requires the source checkout")
  fp <- file.path(PKG, "tests", "testthat", "fixtures",
                  "sigprofiler_sbs96_specimen.txt")
  if (!file.exists(fp)) stop("specimen fixture missing: ", fp)
  fp
})
```

## Install

msuiter is a source install: the numerical kernels are a Rust workspace that
`R CMD INSTALL` builds through the package `configure` face, so the toolchain
floors stated in DESCRIPTION bind the install itself. The committed renv
lockfile pins the R and package universe the campaign is validated against;
restoring it before installing keeps the floor question answered by bytes
rather than by luck.

```{r install-face}
if (!is.na(PKG)) {
  desc <- readLines(file.path(PKG, "DESCRIPTION"), warn = FALSE)
  print(desc[grepl("^Package:|^Version:|^Depends:|^SystemRequirements:",
                   desc)])
  lockfile <- file.path(PKG, "inst", "repro", "renv.lock")
  if (file.exists(lockfile)) {
    print(basename(lockfile))
  } else if (!dir.exists(file.path(PKG, "inst", "repro"))) {
    # inst/repro ships inside the source package, so this branch is the
    # synthetic-root face of the governing test rather than a real build
    # context; say so rather than stopping.
    print("renv.lock: outside this build context")
  } else {
    stop("committed renv lockfile missing from its own committed directory")
  }
} else {
  print("install face reads the source DESCRIPTION")
}
```

With a checkout in hand, the install face is one command:

```{sh, eval = FALSE}
R CMD INSTALL msuiter   # from the source root; configure builds the Rust core
```

Without a checkout, install the development build straight from GitHub -- the
same `configure` face builds the Rust core on the way in:

```{sh, eval = FALSE}
Rscript -e 'remotes::install_github("WangLabCSU/msuiter")'
```

Prebuilt packages are attached to the tagged release and install from a local
file with `install.packages(<file>, repos = NULL)`. There is no CRAN release
yet.

## Five-minute path

Real signature analyses ask two questions: *which* mutational processes
shaped this cohort, and *how much* did each contribute to each sample? The
five-minute path answers both on data whose truth is known in advance, so
every number printed below is a real answer you can check against the ground
truth that was planted.

The path runs in five faces. It plants a ground truth taken from the bundled
COSMIC v3.6 reference database -- the reference ships inside the package, so
the trusted default needs no download -- then discovers signatures from the
simulation alone, checks the discovery against the truth, refits every sample
against the known dictionary, and shows how the number of processes is argued
rather than guessed.

### Plant a ground truth

The bundled reference database carries five dictionaries: small-variant SBS
and DBS dictionaries for the two human genome builds, plus the indel
dictionary. Take the human GRCh38 SBS dictionary and keep its first three
signatures -- these are the processes the rest of the path must recover.

```{r refdb}
br <- ms_refdb_bundled()
print(br)
```

```{r sigs}
S <- br[["SBS_GRCh38"]]@matrices[[1]][, 1:3]
colnames(S)
```

Now the planting pattern: three kinds of simulated samples, each dominated by
one of the three processes, so the right answer is known before any software
runs.

```{r plant}
pat <- matrix(c(0.8, 0.1, 0.1,
                0.1, 0.8, 0.1,
                0.1, 0.1, 0.8), 3, 3)
E <- pat[, rep(1:3, each = 8)]
colnames(E) <- paste0("S", 1:24)
```

`ms_simulate()` turns ground truth plus exposures into a catalog a real
pipeline could have produced -- channels by samples, the shape every
downstream face speaks:

```{r simulate}
sim <- ms_simulate(S, exposures = E, burden = 20000, seed = 1)
sim
```

### Discover, then check against the truth

```{r extract}
ext <- ms_extract(sim, k = 3)
ext
```

`ms_extract()` ran the ensemble-plus-consensus pipeline and returned three de
novo signatures, discovered from the catalog alone. We told it how many to
look for -- in a real analysis you would not know, and `ms_select_k()` below
is the evidence panel that argues the choice.

`ms_compare()` scores every discovered signature against every reference
signature, calibrates each score against a null distribution, and assigns
matches so each reference is claimed at most once:

```{r compare}
cmp <- ms_compare(ext@signatures, S,
                  exposures_est = ext@exposures, exposures_ref = E,
                  null_n = 200, null_n_draws = 500, seed = 1L)
cmp
round(cmp@metrics$cosine, 3)
print(cmp@hungarian)
```

The diagonal similarities sit near one: all three planted processes were
recovered, none were confused with one another, and the exposure-level test
rides along in the same comparison object.

### Refit with the known dictionary

Discovery finds the processes; fitting answers *how much of each* is in
every sample. `ms_fit()` regresses each sample's catalog on the known
dictionary under a non-negativity constraint, and the support table flags
which exposures are statistically real rather than noise:

```{r fit}
fit <- ms_fit(sim, S, method = "nnls")
fit
round(fit@exposures[, c("S1", "S9", "S17")], 1)
head(fit@support, 4L)
```

Read one column and the planting comes back: each sample draws about four
fifths of its mutations from its dominant process, and the support table
agrees that the two minor contributions are real but small.

### Argue the number of processes

The extraction above was told how many processes to look for; a real
analysis must argue that number. `ms_select_k()` crosses a grid of candidate
counts, measures reconstruction error and stability across replicates, and
vetoes unstable answers -- the evidence table is the argument, and only one
row survives:

```{r select-k}
ksel <- ms_select_k(sim, k_grid = 2:4, replicates = 4, k_folds = 3,
                    n_seeds = 2, seed = 1)
ksel$k
ksel$k_evidence[, c("k", "cv_test_mse", "avg_stability",
                    "min_cluster_stability", "passes_veto", "selected")]
```

### Bringing real data in

Simulations prove the machinery; real analyses start from files. The
committed specimen fixture is a SigProfiler-format probability table, and
`ms_import()` reads it into the same typed object the extraction produced.
The `kind` argument is the routing rule: a catalog is mutation counts, a
signature dictionary is probabilities.

```{r import}
imp <- ms_import(FIX, format = "sigprofiler", kind = "signatures")
imp
```

## Anatomy of the output

Every face above returned a typed object, not a loose matrix. The class name
says what you are holding; the slots carry the pieces -- the matrices, the
engine and the seed that produced them, the metadata each boundary validated
on the way in. Print the object for the one-line summary; reach into the
slots when a figure or a table needs the raw pieces.

```{r anatomy}
print(class(sim))
print(class(ext))
print(class(cmp))
print(class(fit))
print(ext@engine)
print(dim(ext@signatures))
```

The engine face names the registered engine that ran the extraction -- the
pluggable registry is what third-party packages extend, and the
[extending guide](extending.html) walks that contract.
